thesis: Even radical rule changes require observable differences and do not erase epistemic or ethical responsibility.
role: Examine pauses, external computation and conscious inhabitants.

ideas.statement: State, parameter and rule interventions differ; universal pauses or slowing leave no trace without an unaffected observation channel.
Simulation moves explanation to another level and internal computation bounds do not automatically apply to external physics.
If implemented beings experience suffering, substrate does not erase moral standing; robust protective decisions remain explicit normative choices.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Consciousness of every program is not assumed, and revision need not eliminate all reliable relationships.
